newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada new health minister to preserve system.
newsitem.headline: Canada new health minister to preserve system.

text.p: Canada's new health minister Allan Rock promised on Wednesday to preserve the country's government-run health care system, but he gave no hint of increased spending.
"The health care system has been a priority to this government at all times," Rock told reporters after he was appointed health minister in Liberal Prime Minister Jean Chretien's new cabinet.

He said his first priority would be to meet with health ministers in the provinces and territories to decide how best to fund the health care system, "to make sure the health care system is strengthened and preserved."
He reminded reporters that the Liberals promised in the election campaign before the June 2 election that they would eliminate planned cuts to health care.
"So there will be a stable floor of very sizeable transfers to the provinces," Rock said.
But he gave no hint of giving in to pressure from some left-leaning Liberals to open up the public purse now that the budget deficit was under control.
Since the election, some of the Liberal caucus have expressed hope that the Liberals would relax their fight to control spending and turn their attention to rejuvenating social programs.
During their previous term in government, the Liberals reduced the deficit to an expected C$15 billion in the fiscal year ended March 31, 1997 from C$42 billion when the Liberals took power in 1993.

The party is being watched carefully to see if it will yield to pressure from its left wing and from social groups to spend more, or if it will heed business groups that advise paying down the debt and cutting taxes.
Conservative Leader Jean Charest criticized the Liberals for showing no direction on Wednesday.
"On issues of jobs and health care, for example, we still don't have any indication of where they are going," Charest told a news conference after the announcement of the new cabinet.
